newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap-Diesel steady, fuel oil soft.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap-Diesel steady, fuel oil soft.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps hovered around its morning levels late Friday amid a relatively inactive market as traders were awaiting fresh indicators from the cash trades, brokers said.
July gasoil swaps were last quoted at $22.35/$22.45 per barrel, August at $22.75/$22.85, little moved from its morning quotes and up about 25 cents from Thursday, brokers said.
Jet/gas oil spreads for August were heard traded at $1.75 and $1.80 around Thursday's quotes.
Prompt July regrade however were slightly firmer from Thursday, riding on back of strong jet prices, traders said.
July regrade was quoted at $2.05/$2.20 up from a bid seen Thursday at $2.00 per barrel.
They said on Thursday, a 130,000 barrel cargo of jet fuel for lifting in July was traded at $24.65 per barrel free-on-board (fob), up 45 cents from Wednesday's traded level.
Traders also said jet demand from Indonesia is picking up.
Indonesia is expected to buy three million barrels for August delivery, up about one million from its normal monthly import.
Traders said gas oil prices were also expected to catch up when Chinese demand returns in August after the Hong Kong handover.
Rumours were also heard that a local trader, long on July paper positions may surface to support physical prices.
Shell Singapore would also maintain run cuts at its 435,000 bpd refinery in July. The refinery is currently running at 58,000 tpd, down from its normal 59,000 tpd.
Traders said the lower output would help support prices.
Fuel oil swaps were unchanged as traders assessed fundamentals in the cash market.
Traders said cash prices had fallen by at least $3 per tonne on Thursday and the undertone is soft.
They were uncertain if prices had fallen due to weaker fundamentals or due to a handful of players who were pricing the market.
The traders said demand is expected to rise in August as Indonesia is expected to import some cargoes with two of their refineries undergo maintenance shutdown.
July was last quoted at $98.50/$99.75 per tonne.
